claims.text: The identity of X controls whether CrFeCoNiX forms a stable protective oxide above 900 °C.
Al forms a low-diffusivity, chemically inert oxide.
Si forms a low-diffusivity, chemically inert oxide.
Selective oxidation of Al in CrFeCoNiAl produces a thin, coherent, low-mismatch oxide that grows slowly without cracking.
Selective oxidation of Si in CrFeCoNiSi produces a thin, coherent, low-mismatch oxide that grows slowly without cracking.
Mn is the major oxide-forming element during oxidation of CrMnFeCoNi.
The Mn oxides formed on CrMnFeCoNi are non-protective.
Mn oxidation is rapid and involves high oxygen diffusivity, producing porous manganese oxides.
The Mn-rich oxide scale loses coherence and consequently cracks or spalls.
The tested CrFeCoNiX alloys have a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state with a uniform elemental distribution.
Oxide persistence is governed by lattice coherence and thermal-expansion matching at the oxide/substrate interface.
Grain-boundary diffusion and interfacial stresses moderate oxide/substrate coherence.
The lower alloy diffusivity and favorable oxidation thermodynamics of Al cause slowly growing, adherent alumina with minimal interfacial strain.
The lower alloy diffusivity and favorable oxidation thermodynamics of Si cause slowly growing, adherent silica or silicate with minimal interfacial strain.
Mn's oxygen affinity and diffusivity cause formation of a non-protective oxide and accelerated degradation.
CrFeCoNiAl will form a thin, uniform, slowly growing, adherent oxide under the specified high-temperature conditions.
CrFeCoNiSi will form a thin, uniform, slowly growing, adherent oxide under the specified high-temperature conditions.
CrFeCoNiMn will form a thicker, less coherent scale that cracks and spalls and causes accelerated degradation.
The hypothesis applies during prolonged exposure at or above 900 °C in oxidizing or corrosive atmospheres.
The hypothesis requires the alloy to remain a single- or multiphase metallic solid solution during prolonged exposure.
